title: FOMC minutes of the September 14-15, 2027 meeting (14:00 ET) — the first prose account of the SEP that introduces the 2030 dot
source: EST: THE BOARD'S OWN RULE, MEASURED RATHER THAN QUOTED. federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm (fetched direct 2026-09-06 by this session, HTTP 200, 164,831 bytes, page stamp 'Last Update: August 19, 2026') states verbatim 'The minutes of regularly scheduled meetings are released three weeks after the date of the policy decision.' This session did not quote it and stop: it parsed all 45 '(Released <Month> <D>, <YYYY>)' strings the page attaches to its own minutes links, paired each to its meeting panel-by-panel, and differenced them. 42 OF 45 SIT AT EXACTLY D+21, AND ALL 42 ARE A WEDNESDAY. The three exceptions are 2023-11-01 -> 2023-11-21 (D+20, Tue), 2024-11-07 -> 2024-11-26 (D+19, Tue) and 2025-12-10 -> 2025-12-30 (D+20, Tue) — every one a late-year release pulled forward off a holiday week, and every one a Tuesday. SEPTEMBER IS CLEAN 5 OF 5 at exactly D+21 on a Wednesday: 2021-09-22 -> 2021-10-13, 2022-09-21 -> 2022-10-12, 2023-09-20 -> 2023-10-11, 2024-09-18 -> 2024-10-09, 2025-09-17 -> 2025-10-08. No US market holiday falls in a September meeting's D+21 week (nyse.com/markets/hours-calendars, HTTP 200, 109,180 bytes this session: the only autumn 2027 NYSE holidays are Labor Day 2027-09-06 and Thanksgiving 2027-11-25). 2027-09-15 + 21 days = Wednesday 2027-10-06. Filed estimate because a measured rule applied to a date the Board itself calls tentative cannot be more confident than its input — the same page states 'Each meeting date is tentative until confirmed at the meeting immediately preceding it', so this date inherits the 2027-07-27/28 confirmation. The 14:00 ET publication time is the standing convention and is not on this page. Discovered during the fomc-2027-09-15 initial research, checked 2026-09-06
notes: PROPOSED by the fomc-2027-09-15 initial research (2026-09-06), and proposed deliberately rather than by default: the seeding proposal proposals/fomc-2027-09-15.from-consumer-confidence-2027-09-28.json explicitly declined to file it and assigned it to this lane in writing ('The minutes are NOT proposed here: the Board's three-week convention ... puts them on Wednesday 2027-10-06, and that is this meeting's lane to file rather than a CB lane's to guess'). This is that filing, on the lane's own re-measurement rather than the proposal's arithmetic. It follows the precedent fomc-2027-07-28 set when it proposed fomc-minutes-2027-08-18 over fomc-2027-06-09's stated objection that a three-week rule on a tentative date is 'two inference layers on a self-disclaimed primary' — the rule is now measured at 42 of 45 with a clean September sub-rule and a holiday explanation covering all three exceptions, and the class is already canonical in this calendar (fomc-minutes-2027-06-30.json, fomc-minutes-2027-08-18.json), so declining would leave a hole rather than hold a line. WHAT MAKES THIS PARTICULAR RELEASE WORTH TRACKING: 2027-09-15 is a SEP meeting and, per the Board's projections FAQ (federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomc_projectionsfaqs.htm, HTTP 200, 84,788 bytes this session), 'The projections made in September and December are for the current year, for the subsequent three years, and for the longer run' — so it publishes 2027/2028/2029/2030 and the longer run, and is the first meeting at which a 2030 dot exists at all. These minutes are the first prose account of how that new terminal column was set. Impact low: minutes are a commentary release, no house playbook (S1/S2/E1/S3/S4 + G1) is rates- or minutes-keyed, and symbols is empty. Estimate widens caution only; nothing here licenses an entry.
